audit.whatIsWrong: content.early explains Sap Magic as "his passive heals back your poke whenever he hits a sapling or you near it". Riot's text: "Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL, this cooldown is reduced." The heal comes off his basic attack, and what accelerates it is being hit by YOUR spells.
audit.why: This inverts the poke plan. Every Shock Blast that lands on Maokai pulls his next Sap Magic heal forward — so a Jayce chipping him constantly is funding the sustain he is trying to out-damage. The correct read is that chip alone genuinely cannot build a lead, and that the poke only converts when it is bundled into a burst window with Grievous Wounds up, not spread across the wave. The page reaches half of that conclusion by accident and gives the wrong reason, which means the reader cannot generalise it.
audit.corrected: Sap Magic described as an attack-heal whose cooldown is pulled forward by your own spell hits, with the poke plan re-keyed to burst windows plus anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built on "bait Twisted Advance, all-in once it is on cooldown" and never once prints that cooldown, or any other.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s at 525 range — a real window, long enough that baiting it genuinely buys you a full trade, which makes the page's central instruction worth following. Bramble Smash at 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s is not: it is back before your combo finishes, so it cannot be baited the same way. Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90s from 3000 range, and Sapling Toss is 18s at 1100 — his only true long-range tool, which is why the level-1 zoning the page describes has a fourteen-second gap in it.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance 14s, Bramble Smash 7s, Sapling Toss 18s at 1100, Nature's Grasp 130s at 3000 written into the spikes, mid and cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven stages carry a different side than the why beneath them. The chart reads Skill, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Jayce, Jayce; the whys read "Maokai owns Level 1", "Even at 2", "Your hardest spike", "Skill window", "You keep 6", "Maokai's first tank item is up... your kill pressure evaporates", "He out-scales hard".
audit.why: Jayce loses this 46.57%, and the chart hands him both item stages — the two the prose explicitly says he loses — while taking level 6 away from him, the one stage the prose calls "your cleanest all-in". Every disagreement points the reader the wrong way.
audit.corrected: Maokai, Skill, Jayce, Skill, Jayce, Maokai, Maokai — exactly what the seven whys say.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics that decide trades are absent. Twisted Advance makes Maokai UNTARGETABLE while he contorts and dashes, and Bramble Smash GROUNDS on top of its knockback and slow.
audit.why: Untargetable means a Shock Blast already in the air or a Thundering Blow queued at him during the dash is simply wasted — you have to spend your answer before he casts or after he arrives, never during, which is the same discipline this matchup asks for everywhere else. Grounding is worse: Jayce's only mobility is To the Skies! and the Hextech Capacitor move speed on a swap, so a Bramble Smash landing on you removes both. The page tells you to "reset the trade on your Hextech Capacitor move-speed burst" immediately after being knocked back by the exact ability that denies it.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance's untargetability and Bramble Smash's grounding written in, with the escape advice corrected.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you out-range him: take Cannon Q and gate-Q his step-ups, because his only answer is a Sapling Toss and a Bramble Smash knockback he has to walk into your range to land. The catch is Sap Magic — his passive heals back your poke whenever he hits a sapling or you near it, so chip alone never builds a real lead. The thing that breaks this lane is Twisted Advance: it is a targeted dash-root, so your Hextech Capacitor move-speed burst cannot dodge it the way it sidesteps a skillshot. Never poke from inside its range, because the root pins you for a free Bramble Smash plus sapling and flips the trade.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you out-range him: take Cannon Q and gate-Q his step-ups, because his only answers are an 18s Sapling Toss and a Bramble Smash he has to walk into your range to land. Sap Magic is the catch, and not for the reason it looks: his attack-heal runs on a cooldown that shortens every time a spell STRIKES him, so your own chip is quietly funding his sustain. Poke to set up one burst window, not to grind him down. And never sit inside 525 — Twisted Advance is a targeted dash-root and he is untargetable the whole way across it, so nothing you throw mid-dash lands.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are your real window — fire Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate for the long-range accelerated orb, and when he steps up to last-hit, Cannon-Q into the swap so the first Hammer hit shreds his armor and MR, then To the Skies into Lightning Field. The whole fight is fought around his Twisted Advance: bait it, sidestep or eat it before you commit, and only all-in once it is on cooldown. At 6 you gain no new burst — your R is the same stance swap you already had, not an ult — but the swap-shred combo plus Thundering Blow knocking him off his Bramble Smash is still your cleanest kill; take it before his armor items come online.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are your real window — gate a Shock Blast for the long-range orb, and on his step-up, Cannon-Q into the swap so the first hit shreds armor and MR, then To the Skies! into Lightning Field. Everything is fought around Twisted Advance at 14s: bait it and you own a full trade, because Bramble Smash at 7s is back before your combo ends and cannot be baited the same way. Do not spend Thundering Blow on the incoming Bramble Smash either — it grounds you, and grounded there is no Capacitor escape to reset into. At 6 you gain no new burst, but this is still your cleanest kill.

notes: MECHANIC ERROR: content.early says Sap Magic "heals back your poke whenever he hits a sapling or you near it". Riot's text is that his basic attack heals him on a moderate cooldown, and that the cooldown is reduced each time he casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL. So Jayce's own poke accelerates the heal — the exact opposite of a mechanic the reader can farm value from. That turns "chip him down" into "poke to set up one burst window, with Grievous Wounds up", and the page reached a similar conclusion by the wrong route, which meant the reader could not apply it anywhere else. MISSING: Twisted Advance makes him UNTARGETABLE across the dash, so an orb in flight or a queued Thundering Blow is wasted if it is aimed at him mid-dash; and Bramble Smash GROUNDS. The grounding one matters most because the page tells you, in wants.you[2], to "reset the trade on your Hextech Capacitor move-speed burst" immediately after eating Bramble Smash — the ability that removes exactly that escape, along with To the Skies!. Cooldowns added: Twisted Advance 14/13/12/11/10s at 525, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14s at 1100, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s at 3000. The 14s-versus-7s contrast is the useful one: Twisted Advance can be baited and Bramble Smash cannot. LEVEL CHART: five of seven stages disagreed with their own whys, including both item stages reading Jayce above "your kill pressure evaporates" and "he out-scales hard" in a matchup Jayce loses 46.57%. Corrected to Maokai/Skill/Jayce/Skill/Jayce/Maokai/Maokai.
